notes: A legendary fly-in destination since the 1960s. Aviation-themed décor and homemade pies — marionberry and rhubarb are the ones to get. Named a Top 10 Airport Restaurant by AOPA. Watch planes taxi past while you eat. Wed–Sun 8AM–4PM.

Amelia Earhart-themed restaurant inside a plane hangar at Bremerton National. American classics with generous portions. Sunday brunch buffet draws pilots and locals alike. Tue–Thu 6AM–8PM · Fri–Sat 6AM–9PM · Sun 6AM–8PM · Closed Mon.
On-field restaurant right at Tacoma Narrows with runway views. Burgers
column13: Cajun tots and Harmon craft beers on tap. Watch GA aircraft and business jets roll by. Open daily 11AM–9PM.

notes: World-famous fly-in fishing resort on the White River. The restaurant serves fresh trout caught steps from the table. One of the most unique fly-in dining experiences in the country — land on the private strip and walk to the table.

Classic airport diner at Chino Airport — home of the Planes of Fame Air Museum. Breakfast and lunch staples served with a side of warbird sightings. A longtime favorite for pilots flying the Southern California basin.
A legendary California pit stop on the I-5 corridor. Land at the private Harris Ranch strip and walk to one of the state's most famous steakhouses. Prime beef raised on-site. Open for breakfast
Popular on-field café at Camarillo Airport serving breakfast and lunch. Generous portions and a friendly pilot crowd. On clear days the Channel Islands are visible from the ramp. Open daily 7AM–3PM.

Upscale dining with panoramic views of the Front Range and runway at Centennial Airport. One of Colorado's best airport restaurants — think steaks and Colorado craft beers with a view of the Rockies. Open for lunch and dinner.

On-field restaurant at Waterbury-Oxford with runway views. Breakfast and lunch served daily. Local favorite for weekend fly-ins in the Connecticut hills. Named for the airport elevation — 726 feet MSL.

Located inside the famous Spruce Creek Fly-In community — one of the largest residential airparks in the world. Casual café atmosphere with a mix of resident pilots and visiting aviators. Great spot to soak up the unique fly-in neighborhood vibe.

A Vero Beach institution right on the airport with sweeping runway views. Known for generous portions of American comfort food and a lively bar. Popular with both Piper training fleet pilots from next door and transient GA traffic.

Casual on-field diner at Winter Haven Regional serving breakfast and lunch. Friendly staff and a loyal local pilot following. Good stopping point between Tampa and Orlando in the heart of central Florida's lake country.

On-field restaurant at Bartow Municipal in the heart of Polk County. Breakfast and lunch with views of the ramp and a rotating menu of daily specials. A quiet alternative to busier central Florida airports.
Relaxed café at Venice Municipal — the shark tooth capital of the world. Breakfast and lunch with a friendly airport crowd. Venice has one of the most active GA communities on Florida's Gulf Coast.

On-field café at Ocala International serving breakfast and lunch to the north-central Florida GA community. Horse country surrounds the airport — a good fuel and food stop between Gainesville and the I-4 corridor.

Waterfront airport restaurant at Albert Whitted with stunning views of Tampa Bay and the St. Pete skyline. One of Florida's most scenic dining spots. Open for breakfast and lunch — arrive early on weekends.
Down-home Florida diner at Okeechobee County Airport. Breakfast and lunch served to a mix of ag pilots
column12: fishermen and cross-country traffic. Okeechobee sits at the north end of the lake — good stopping point for south Florida trips.

notes: Casual café at Fort Lauderdale Executive — one of the busiest GA airports in the country. Breakfast and lunch with a front-row seat to a parade of jets
column12: turboprops and helicopters. Great people-watching between bites.

notes: WWII-themed restaurant adjacent to DeKalb-Peachtree with a control tower you can dine in. Runway views
column12: wartime memorabilia and a full menu of American classics. One of the most atmospheric airport-adjacent restaurants in the Southeast.

notes: Beloved on-field diner at Schaumburg Regional in the Chicago suburbs. Big breakfasts
column12: burgers and a loyal pilot crowd. One of the busiest small GA airports in Illinois — expect company on weekend mornings.

notes: Waterfront restaurant on Eagle Creek Reservoir adjacent to Eagle Creek Airpark. Seafood
column12: burgers and lake views. A fun combination of the boating and flying communities in one spot on the west side of Indianapolis.

notes: Historic hotel café at a private Kansas airstrip. The Beaumont Hotel dates to 1879 and has hosted cattle drives and oil barons. A genuine step back in time — land at the grass strip and walk to the dining room.

French bistro in the historic terminal at Bowman Field — one of the oldest operating airports in the US. White tablecloths and classic French cuisine next to a ramp full of vintage aircraft. A genuinely surprising find at a Kentucky GA airport.

Classic New England airport diner at Minute Man Airfield west of Boston. Famous among local pilots for generous breakfasts and friendly service. The airfield has strong ties to the local Civil Air Patrol and EAA community.
On-field restaurant at Nantucket Memorial with views of one of the most scenic GA airports on the East Coast. Breakfast and lunch — expect a mix of island residents
column12: ferry commuters and summer transient traffic from throughout the Northeast.

notes: Upscale farm-to-table dining in the historic Holman Field terminal building overlooking the Mississippi River and downtown St. Paul skyline. One of the most architecturally beautiful airport restaurants in the Midwest. Lunch and dinner.

A genuine BBQ landmark accessible only by air or a bumpy dirt road. Fly into this grass strip in the North Carolina Sandhills and taxi up to a pulled pork sandwich that's worth the trip. A bucket-list fly-in for East Coast pilots. Thu–Sun only.

On-field diner at Cape May Airport on the southern tip of New Jersey. Breakfast and lunch served to a mix of shore-bound vacationers and transient GA traffic. One of the more scenic GA airports in the mid-Atlantic.

On-field café at Gabreski Airport on Long Island's East End — gateway to the Hamptons. Breakfast and lunch with ramp views. A popular fuel and food stop for NYC-area pilots heading out to eastern Long Island.

Beloved Hudson Valley airport diner at Sky Acres. Breakfast and lunch served to a tight-knit local flying community. The airport has one of the most active pilot communities in the mid-Hudson Valley. Worth the trip from NYC.

On-field restaurant at Lunken Airport — one of the oldest airports in the country — with art deco terminal views and a classic American menu. Breakfast and lunch. A beloved institution for the Cincinnati aviation community.
Named for the Ford Tri-Motor
column12: this diner at Erie-Ottawa International sits on the shores of Lake Erie. Breakfast and lunch with lake views. Port Clinton is the walleye capital of the world — fish specials are a regular feature.

notes: Down-home Oklahoma diner at Ardmore Municipal with a devoted local following. Breakfast and lunch at a price that makes you feel like you're back in 1985. A good fuel stop on the I-35 corridor between Oklahoma City and Dallas.
Upscale Italian steakhouse at Arnold Palmer Regional — fittingly
column12: in the hometown of the King himself. One of the more elegant airport restaurants in the Northeast. Dinner-focused with a full bar and sweeping views of the Laurel Highlands.

notes: On-field café at Greenville Downtown with ramp views and a loyal local pilot crowd. Breakfast and lunch in the heart of the South Carolina Upstate. The airport sits minutes from downtown Greenville — one of the most revitalized mid-size cities in the Southeast.
A Texas institution. The Southern Flyer is one of the most talked-about airport diners in the state — chicken fried steak
column12: jalapeño cornbread and sweet tea. Brenham is Blue Bell ice cream country. Breakfast and lunch Fri–Sun. Worth planning a trip around.

notes: On-field café at Garner Field in the Texas Hill Country. Breakfast and lunch with a strong local ranching and hunting crowd. Uvalde is one of the highest-density quail hunting areas in Texas — expect to share the ramp with hunting camp traffic in season.
One of Texas's most celebrated BBQ joints — brisket
column12: ribs and sausage cooked over mesquite in open pits out front. A short drive from Stephenville Clark Regional in the heart of Cowboy Country. The smell hits you a mile out. Open daily.

notes: On-field restaurant at Hooks — one of the busiest GA airports in the Houston metro. Breakfast and lunch with ramp views of a constant stream of GA traffic. A reliable fuel-and-food stop north of Houston.

The airport is named after the restaurant — that's how good the catfish is. Land at this Texas private strip and walk to one of the state's most unique dining experiences. A genuine Texas original that's been drawing pilots for decades.

Upscale restaurant at Scottsdale Airport with sweeping desert views and a sleek modern interior. One of the most polished airport dining experiences in the Southwest. Lunch and dinner — expect a sophisticated crowd and a serious cocktail program.
Perched on top of the Sedona Airport mesa at 4
column12: 800 feet with arguably the most dramatic views of any airport restaurant in the country. Red rock formations in every direction. Breakfast and lunch — arrive early before the tour helicopter traffic picks up.
